# Native mdoc document-signing source check — 2026-11-24

This note separates source-backed mdoc behavior from the independent application choices in `draft.md`. It is research evidence, not a claim of ISO conformance or a proposed change to ISO mdoc. The pinned public WG10 PDF was fetched directly from its commit URL; its 2,697,049 bytes hash to SHA-256 `86a1e8356096923bb9293b1582e69193eff724d8fabf7cfe94ef97bf104b3426`, matching `sources.json`. Page references below are **PDF page numbers**. The PDF is linked, not copied here.

## Source boundary

| Source | Verified status and usable conclusion |

Its public abstract covers obtaining mDL data, tying it to the holder, and authenticating origin and integrity. The licensed complete 2021 text was **not** reviewed here, so no clause-level assertion below is attributed to the published edition. ISO currently lists a DIS successor under development. |

## Distinct authentication acts

1. **Issuer authentication:** The WG10 working text §§12.3.1–12.3.5 (PDF pp. 55–59) has the issuing authority sign the MSO in `IssuerAuth` and has the reader verify the signature, certificate, returned item digests, document type and validity (§12.8.1, PDF p. 70). The MSO carries `deviceKeyInfo.deviceKey`; issuer item digests cover encoded `IssuerSignedItemBytes`, including tag 24 (§12.3.5, PDF p. 59). The working text permits partial item disclosure for presentation, so requiring every item named by the MSO is this signing profile's issuance-completeness rule, not an mdoc presentation rule. [WG10 pinned PDF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ISOWG10/ISO-18013/b250e7a64f99e22ceed10d2a5799bed38ee89f85/Working%20Documents/Working%20Draft%20ISO_IEC_18013-5_second-edition_CD_ballot_resolution_v4.pdf).
2. **Holder/device authentication:** Working-text §12.4 (PDF pp. 62–63) authenticates a `DeviceAuthenticationBytes` structure containing the session transcript, document type and device namespaces. Its `DeviceMac` or `DeviceSignature` uses the MSO-certified device key and a detached COSE payload. A valid device presentation therefore proves that particular session/device response, not a free-standing signature over arbitrary supplied document bytes. The working text's informative Annex D.7.2 (PDF pp. 151–152) does give an **example** of signing a document hash as an authorized `DeviceSigned` data element in a request/response. That example remains within device authentication and does not specify the independent certified document key or standalone artifact selected by this profile. [WG10 pinned PDF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ISOWG10/ISO-18013/b250e7a64f99e22ceed10d2a5799bed38ee89f85/Working%20Documents/Working%20Draft%20ISO_IEC_18013-5_second-edition_CD_ballot_resolution_v4.pdf).
3. **Document signature:** [RFC 9052 §§4.2–4.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9052.html#section-4.2) supplies a single-signer COSE_Sign1 with `nil` payload for detached content. Its `Signature1` input binds the protected-header bytes, external AAD and **exact detached payload bytes**. It does not confer document-signing authority or bind an mdoc credential by itself. Requiring an issuer-authenticated separate key, exact purpose and profile, and protected SHA-512 binding to the complete original credential is the experimental contract. Critical-header processing follows [RFC 9052 §3.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9052.html#section-3.1); the exact custom label and first-in-`crit` order are additional profile rules.

For a bounded holder proof, the exact working-text device structure matters. §10.3.3 (PDF p. 37) defines `DeviceSigned` as `nameSpaces: DeviceNameSpacesBytes` plus `deviceAuth`; `DeviceNameSpacesBytes` is tag 24 around a byte string containing CBOR `DeviceNameSpaces`. The text expressly permits `DeviceNameSpaces` to be an empty map. §12.4.4 (PDF pp. 62–63) defines `DeviceAuthenticationBytes = #6.24(bstr .cbor ["DeviceAuthentication", SessionTranscript, DocType, DeviceNameSpacesBytes])`; §12.4.6 (PDF p. 64) puts its signature in untagged COSE_Sign1 with a **null** payload, this tagged byte string as detached content, zero-length external AAD, and protected algorithm. Under [RFC 9052 §4.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9052.html#section-4.4), ES256 verification signs `Sig_structure = ["Signature1", exact protected bstr, h'', exact DeviceAuthenticationBytes]` with the MSO device key. Selecting only empty `DeviceNameSpaces` is a defensible narrower **experimental** holder-authentication primitive, provided the session transcript is real and the document type and original tagged bytes are checked. It gives no document-signing privilege. [WG10 pinned PDF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ISOWG10/ISO-18013/b250e7a64f99e22ceed10d2a5799bed38ee89f85/Working%20Documents/Working%20Draft%20ISO_IEC_18013-5_second-edition_CD_ballot_resolution_v4.pdf).

## Certificate authority and key contract

The WG10 working text places the issuer certificate in `x5chain` and validates it under the mDL certificate/role profile (§12.3.4 and Annex B, PDF pp. 58–59, 84). [RFC 9360 §2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9360.html#section-2) defines `x5chain` (33) as candidate chain material and explicitly treats carried certificates as **untrusted input**; it defines `x5t` (34) as a DER-certificate thumbprint, not trust. The application must separately admit a signing issuer/root, role, document type and profile. Accepting a government mDL or photoID as enrollment identity evidence does **not** appoint that identity issuer as a document-signing CA or import its root into a different issuance chain. This last sentence is a policy inference from the separate trust functions, not an ISO clause. [RFC 5280 §4.2.1.12](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.2.1.12) further makes certificate key usage/purpose an explicit application validation concern.

The working text recommends protected `x5t` and permits a protected `x5chain` reader path, while preserving unprotected `x5chain` issuance for backward compatibility (§12.3.4, PDF pp. 58–59). Requiring protected SHA-256 `x5t` on every signing credential is a stricter profile selection; neither `x5t` nor matching certificate bytes alone authorizes an issuer. The working text allows more issuer algorithms and digest algorithms than this implementation selects (§§12.3.4–12.3.5, PDF pp. 58–59). [RFC 9053 §2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9053.html#section-2.1) maps ES256 to COSE `-7` and defines fixed-width `r || s` ECDSA signatures. [RFC 9881 §4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9881.html#section-4) defines ML-DSA public-key SPKI encoding; [RFC 9964 §§5, 8.1.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9964.html#section-5) registers COSE `-49`/`-50` for ML-DSA-65/87, with empty context and 3,309/4,627-byte signatures. Choosing a distinct ML-DSA-65/87 document key as the complete base is a profile choice, not an ISO mdoc key requirement.

## Status boundary

The WG10 working text places optional MSO `status` in the MSO and describes CWT/COSE MSO revocation lists, including identifier-list or status-list mechanisms (§12.3.6, PDF pp. 59–62). It references Token Status List draft 12. This profile instead uses an issuer-authenticated **namespace item** and selects JWT status lists under [Token Status List draft 21](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-oauth-status-list-21#section-5.1), currently an Internet-Draft in the RFC Editor queue. Draft 21 provides JWT `typ=statuslist+jwt`, URI/index, signed status token and validation rules; its broader options do not imply automatic compatibility with the WG10 MSO/CWT binding. The profile's pinned HTTPS URI, ES256 signer, 300-second limits, one-bit list and explicit status-authority decision are local restrictions. A bit and a backdated evaluation clock do not by themselves establish historical coverage; draft 21's [§8.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-oauth-status-list-21#section-8.3) distinguishes current from historical status.

## Actionable reject-vector boundaries

The existing base vectors cover byte changes, issuer signature/digest failure, certificate substitution, missing protected binding, purpose/profile/mode changes, detached signature changes, missing or conflicting status, and unknown critical headers. Further boundaries to retain or evaluate are:

| Boundary | Re-signed or otherwise valid-looking negative case | Expected decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Enrollment provenance versus CA authority | External identity credential validates under an admitted identity root, while the signing credential is issued by that root without independent document-signing issuer admission. | Reject issuer authorization even when identity proof is valid. |
| Separate document key and purpose | Issuer-authenticated claims name a holder/device key while the required independent PQ profile is selected; or name a distinct key but omit `DOCUMENT_SIGN`. | Reject key mode/purpose before treating a valid detached signature as authority. |
| Exact credential binding | Re-encode semantically equivalent original `IssuerSigned` bytes and retain a valid document signature over its old credential hash. | Reject complete-original-credential binding. |
| Distinct cryptographic acts | Supply a valid `DeviceSignature` over `DeviceAuthenticationBytes` or the Annex D.7.2 style document-hash response in place of this profile's detached document COSE. | Reject as a document signature under this profile. |
| Status representation and time | Put status only at MSO `status`, supply a WG10 CWT list to the JWT selector, or use a current list to assert undocumented historical coverage. | `UNSUPPORTED` for unselected wire method; indeterminate for missing historical coverage. |
| Certificate carriage and role | Valid `IssuerAuth` signature with same-key alternate DER certificate, unprotected/changed `x5t`, or a valid path whose admitted role/document type differs. | Reject thumbprint or authorization as appropriate. |

Treat the expected classification above as a proposed local profile test oracle, not a normative ISO outcome. In particular, cryptographic validity, an identity match, and possession of an mdoc device key are three separate facts from authorization to issue a document-signing credential or sign an arbitrary document.
